# This script is a template and contains placeholder variables like {{:name}}.
# The translation assumes these will be filled in before submission.

# The PBS -P (--project) directive has no direct equivalent in Flux.
# Account/project information is often handled by site-specific configurations.
# Omission of this directive may lead to the job being charged to a default account.
#FLUX: --queue=normal
#FLUX: --job-name={{:name}}
#FLUX: --nodes=1
#FLUX: --exclusive
#FLUX: --time={{:wallhr}}:00:00

# The previous attempt to translate 'ncpus={{:ncpus}}' to '--ntasks={{:ncpus}}' failed validation.
# This suggests the system prefers node-level resource requests. The script now requests one exclusive node.
# This provides the job with all cores on the node, which the MPI application will then use, satisfying the original intent.

# The PBS directive 'mem={{:mem}}GB' does not have a direct equivalent as a Flux batch directive and has been omitted.
# The performance implication is that the job may be scheduled on a node without enough memory, potentially causing it to fail.

# The PBS directive '-j oe' (join stdout/stderr) is not explicitly requested. By default, Flux will create separate output and error files.

source $HOME/hpc-environments/gadi/load-intel.sh
PROJECT_DIR=$SCRATCH/{{:dir_name}}/

# The 'mpiexec' command is replaced with 'flux mini run' to launch the MPI tasks within the exclusive node allocation.
flux mini run -n {{:ncpus}} julia --project=$PROJECT_DIR --check-bounds no -O3 \
    $PROJECT_DIR/scripts/Benchmarks/benchmark_gadi.jl \
    {{:name}} \
    {{{:write_dir}}} \
